relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Bachelor of Arts in Religion and Political Science
relations.evidence: He completed a Bachelor of Arts in both Religion and Political Science from the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa (1990)

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Master of Arts in Political Science
relations.evidence: followed by a Master of Arts in Political Science from the same university (1991).

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: He obtained a Ph.D. in Political Science from Rutgers University, with a focus on political theory, comparative politics, and American politics.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: Steger began his academic career as a Lecturer in Political Science at Rutgers University (1992–95).

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: After a brief stint as Visiting Assistant Professor of Politics at Whitman College (1995–6)

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Assistant Professor of Politics and Government
relations.evidence: he joined Illinois State University as an Assistant Professor of Politics and Government (1996–1999).

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: There, he was promoted to Associate Professor (1999–2003)

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: and then Professor of Politics and Government (2003–2005).

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Professor of Global Studies at the School of Global, Urban and Social Studies
relations.evidence: From 2005 to 2011, he held an appointment as the Professor of Global Studies at the School of Global, Urban and Social Studies at RMIT University, Melbourne, Australia.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: In 2011, he joined the faculty of the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa, where he served as a Professor of Political Science until 2016.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: Since 2016, he has held the position of Professor of Sociology at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: In March 2016, Steger served as the Eccles Distinguished Visiting Scholar at Southern Utah University.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: Additionally, he was appointed as an Honorary Professor of Global Studies at RMIT University from 2015 to 2018

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Distinguished Global Fellow in the Center for Advanced Studies
relations.evidence: held the position of Distinguished Global Fellow in the Center for Advanced Studies at EURAC Research in 2021

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.role: Global Professorial Fellow in the Institute for Culture & Society
relations.evidence: served as a Global Professorial Fellow in the Institute for Culture & Society at Western Sydney University, from 2019 to 2022.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: Together with Terrell Carver, he is the book series editor of Globalization, which has resulted in 30 books on the subject.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: In 1981, Steger initiated his Zen training in Austria under Genro Koudela at the Bodhidharma Zendo in Vienna

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: Later, in 1986, he continued his training with Robert Baker Aitken at the Diamond Sangha in Honolulu, Hawaii, where he completed his formal koan practice.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: together with his wife Perle Besserman, established the Princeton Area Zen Group, where he assumed the role of the group's first teacher.

relations.subject: Manfred B. Steger
relations.evidence: He and Besserman collaborated on several books about lay Zen practice, notably including Grassroots Zen: Community and Practice in the Twenty-First Century and Zen Radicals, Rebels, and Reformers".
